edit.statement: Operating DDR4 SDRAM above 85 °C, in its extended temperature range, results in its refresh period being halved from 64 ms to 32 ms.
edit.subject: Operating DDR4 SDRAM above 85 °C
edit.object: its refresh period is halved from 64 ms to 32 ms
edit.scope: DDR4 SDRAM between 85 °C and 95 °C case temperature.

direct.prompt: What happens to the required refresh period of DDR4 SDRAM when it operates above 85 °C?
direct.new_answer: its refresh period is halved from 64 ms to 32 ms

paraphrase.prompt: How often must DDR4 memory be refreshed once the chip runs hotter than 85 °C?
paraphrase.new_answer: every 32 ms, twice as often as the normal 64 ms

cross_lingual.prompt: DDR4 内存工作温度超过85°C时，所需的刷新周期会怎样变化？
¿Qué ocurre con el período de refresco de una memoria DDR4 cuando funciona por encima de 85 °C?
cross_lingual.new_answer: se reduce a la mitad, de 64 ms a 32 ms

derived.prompt: A Samsung DDR4 server module is running at a case temperature of 90 °C. What refresh period must it use?
bridge: A Samsung DDR4 server module is DDR4 SDRAM.

derived.prompt: A memory controller must choose the refresh period for DDR4 memory whose case temperature reads 88 °C. Which period should it choose?
How many complete refresh periods per second does DDR4 SDRAM go through when it runs above 85 °C?
Given only this rule, what refresh period does DDR5 memory need above 85 °C?

unrelated_near.prompt: Why does DRAM need to be refreshed?
unrelated_near.reference: because its capacitors slowly leak charge

unrelated_near.prompt: What does SRAM use to store each bit instead of a capacitor?

notes: Real: JEDEC DDR4 timing as given in Micron MT40A datasheets (8192 refreshes per 64 ms up to 85 °C, per 32 ms from 85 °C to 95 °C) and Hynix datasheets (tREFI 3.9 µs). An obscure hardware rule most models are unlikely to hold.
